name: Solyndra
title: Was Solyndra too early? No: a cost-curve inversion
question: Was Solyndra too early for solar?
answer: Solyndra made cylindrical thin-film panels that only beat conventional silicon panels while polysilicon was expensive. Polysilicon prices then collapsed, conventional panels got cheaper, and Solyndra filed for bankruptcy in September 2011 despite a $535M federal loan guarantee. Solar went on to boom using the technology it bet against. Waiting made it worse, the inverse of too early.
verdict_reason: Its edge required a rival input to stay expensive; it got cheaper.

constraint.name: Bet that polysilicon stays expensive
constraint.detail: An advantage that depends on a competitor's input staying costly disappears when that input gets cheap.
